html:
The Albanian Declaration of Independence was proclaimed in Vlorë on 28 November 1912 by an assembly of delegates led by Ismail Qemali, during the First Balkan War.

Serbian, Montenegrin and Greek armies were taking Ottoman lands where Albanians lived, and the delegates declared independence to keep them from being divided up. The great powers recognised an Albanian state in 1913, under pressure from Austria and Italy, but left Kosovo and other Albanian lands outside it, almost half of all Albanians. A German prince, William of Wied, ruled for six months in 1914 before World War I brought occupation. The day is Albania's Flag Day, building on the League of Prizren and the work of the alphabet congress.
